<reason>A built the stronger portfolio-renewal case and answered why cheap discovery does not necessarily substitute for mid-budget execution. B raised legitimate marketing-cost and marginal-investment objections, but repeatedly substituted unsupported categorical claims and demands for numerical precision for comparative analysis. A also directly rebutted the status-quo charge by distinguishing selection standards from spending allocation; B merely repeated it. A’s limited demonstration of current underinvestment keeps the win competitive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A exposed that B’s production-and-marketing example could not establish a required hit rate without success payoffs, failure losses, and comparable sequel returns. B subsequently portrayed this justified rejection of false precision as refusing arithmetic, rather than resolving the missing comparison.</best_rebuttal>
